analysis.title: Duttenhoefer's Daily 02.11.2026
key_insights: S&P 500 closed the week at 7580 (+11% YTD) after another difficult week. SOX fell 7% and is now below its 200-day moving average. The Nasdaq vs equal-weighted S&P had its worst month of underperformance since 2002.
Cross-asset levels: US 10yr at 4.93%, Brent $109, Gold $3914, Bitcoin $78k. The GS NeoClouds basket lost 9% on the week. Kospi is trading +2.5%, with SK Hynix +4% and Samsung +2%.
The week ahead is heavy: about 20% of the S&P 500 reports (Apple and Palantir today, AMD tomorrow), US midterm elections are tomorrow, and the jobs report (NFP) is on Friday.

US midterms: prediction markets imply more than 90% odds that Democrats win the House and more than 65% that they win the Senate. Under a Democratic majority the main legislative focus would be fiscal deadlines (spending authority extension and a debt limit increase). GS does not expect major fiscal policy changes over the next two years, but spending could increase.

GS raised its Brent forecasts to $105/bbl for Dec 2026 (from $90) and to $88 for the FY27 average (from $80). Substantial downside supply risks should sustain a large near-term risk premium. The base case now includes a 1mb/d global supply disruption allowance in 2027.
GS's Brent upside scenario is $140/bbl if 2027 average Gulf output stays 3.5mb/d below its 2025 average, versus 1.1mb/d above in the base case.
Russia x Ukraine: a large Ukrainian drone attack significantly damaged an industrial facility in Kstovo, ranked Russia's fourth-largest refinery.

Trades GS is playing into the midterms: long the ACA Beneficiaries basket (GSHLCACA) on a Democratic sweep, long AI Power (GSENEPOW) over ex-Power AI hardware (GSTMTAIH), and the Corporate tax basket (GSPUTAXP).

Earnings: with 60% of S&P 500 companies reported, 3Q26 EPS growth is on track for 33% y/y, matching Q2 as the strongest quarter in recent decades outside post-recession recoveries. The pace of upward revisions has slowed. GS reads 3Q results as supporting continued AI investment growth, with the growth rate of AI capex peaking.

Meta: reportedly built a prototype humanoid robot, internally codenamed Max, with Chinese robotics firm Fourier in roughly three months. S&P revised the credit outlook to negative, citing uncertainty over how long capex stays elevated and how long free operating cash flow stays negative.

Apollo pushes back on the K-shaped consumer narrative. Fed data show nominal spending growing roughly 4-5% y/y across income groups since 2024, and household net worth has risen across the distribution since 2019, including around 80% for the bottom 20%.

Microsoft CEO Nadella (20VC podcast) argues most AI token usage will become a commodity, enterprise value comes from retaining their own knowledge, more capable models are not automatically safer, and larger training budgets must be funded by real revenue and faster economic growth.

GS Tech takeaways this week: the financing needed for AI may be less than investors expect because of levers such as bring-your-own-hardware and vendor prepayment, the market is deep enough for new IG issuance, and enterprise token demand may step up again in 2027.

GS AI adoption tracker: adoption by US firms rose 0.8 points to 24.6% and is expected to reach 28.6% in the next 6 months. Adoption is approaching 50% in information, professional and finance sectors.
G10 consumers continue to benefit from healthy balance sheets and labor markets, but real income growth remains soft in most developed markets.
Kalshi raised $1bn at a $40bn valuation in a round led by Wellington and Sequoia.
Crypto: the FBI attributed the hack of Binance (more than $6bn) to North Korean group TraderTraitor.
GS's Risk Appetite Indicator saw the largest drop in global risk appetite since November 2021 last month.
Reddit CEO on the earnings call: AI Mode does not drive traffic, whereas Google search used to be a traffic driver.
